mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (سأل): for whoever drops the hamza, it admits three aspects. The first is that it is from asking (السؤال), but the hamza has been replaced by an alif; this is a replacement not according to analogy, yet it is permissible; Sībawayh and others reported it. The second is that the alif replaces a wāw: Sībawayh and others reported (سلت تسال) as a dialect, on the pattern of (خفت تخاف). The third aspect is that the alif replaces a yāʾ, from (سال يسيل) "to flow", on the pattern of (كال يكيل). The origin of (سأل), when it is from asking, is that it takes two objects, as in His saying (فلا تسألن ما ليس), and it may be limited to one, like (أعطيت) and (كسوت), as in His saying, the Exalted: (واسألوا ما أنفقتم). When you limit it to one, it may pass by a preposition to that one, as in His saying, the Exalted: (سأل سائل بعذاب), its implied form being "An asker asked the Prophet about a punishment", and the bāʾ means (عن). If you make (سال) from flowing (السيل), the bāʾ does not mean (عن) but is in its own proper sense, its origin being for transitivity. As for the hamza in (سائل), it admits three aspects: the first, that it is original, from asking; the second, that it replaces a wāw, according to the dialect of those who say (سلت تسال) like (خفت تخاف); and the third, that it replaces a yāʾ, if you make (سال) from flowing.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (يوم تكون السماء): the governor of the adverbial is (نراه). It may also be a badal (substitute) from (قريب), the governor of (قريب) being (نراه). It is also said that the governor is (يبصرونهم). The hāʾ and mīm in (يبصرونهم) refer back to the disbelievers and the nominative pronoun to the believers, i.e. the believers see the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, that is, they see them and look at them in the Fire. It is also said that it refers back to (الحميم), which has a plural meaning, i.e. each close friend sees his close friend. It is also said that both pronouns refer back to the disbelievers, i.e. the followers see those they followed in the Fire.

mekki-muskil:15-16.t: His saying (إنها لظى نزاعة): (لظى) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), in the position of the nominative, and (نزاعة) is a second khabar. It is also said that (لظى) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in (إنها), and (نزاعة) is the khabar, in the position of the nominative. It is also said that (لظى) is the khabar of (إن) and (نزاعة) is a badal from (لظى), or nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also said that the pronoun in (إنها) is the pronoun of the story, (لظى) is a mubtadaʾ, (نزاعة) is the khabar of (لظى), and the clause is the khabar of (إن). Whoever reads (نزاعة) in the accusative takes it as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is the reading of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim [Translator's note: the printed text has «خفص»; Ḥafṣ is meant]. The governor of (نزاعة) is what the speech indicates of the meaning of blazing, as if He said: "No! It blazes while stripping away the scalps." Al-Mubarrad denied the permissibility of the accusative of (نزاعة) and said: Laẓā is never anything but a stripper of scalps, so there is no sense in a ḥāl; a ḥāl is only for what may be and may not be. This is the meaning of his statement. [Makkī says:] The ḥāl here is permissible because it confirms what precedes it, as He said: (وهو الحق مصدقا), and the truth is never anything but confirming; and the Exalted said: (وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما), and the path of Allah, exalted be His mention, is never anything but straight. So it is not necessary that the ḥāl be only for a thing that may be and may not be; this is a principle that does not hold in every place, so his statement is not good. It has also been said that this is only an announcement to someone who thought that it would not be, so the ḥāl is sound on this view without objection.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (تدعو من أدبر): a third khabar (predicate) of (إن); or, if you wish, you may cut it off from what precedes it.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying (خلق هلوعا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (خلق), and it is the anticipated ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muqaddara), because anxiety only arises in him after his creation, not at the time of his creation.
His saying (جزوعا) and (منوعا): the khabar (predicate) of an implied (كان), i.e. "he becomes impatient" and "he becomes withholding", or "he turns" and the like. It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of (هلوع), but that is far-fetched, because you would be intending it to come before (إذا).

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying (فمال الذين كفروا): (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الذين) is the khabar (predicate). (مهطعين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it governs (قبلك); (قبلك) is an adverbial of place.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying (عزين): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) as well, from (الذين). It is the plural of (عزة). It was pluralised with wāw and nūn, although it is feminine and not rational, so that this would be a compensation for what was deleted from it. It is said that its origin is (عزهة), just as the origin of (سنة) is (سنهة); then the hāʾ was deleted, and its plural with wāw and nūn was made a compensation for the deletion.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying (يوم يخرجون): (يوم) is a badal (substitute) from (يومهم), and (يومهم) is accusative governed by (يلاقوا) as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
His saying (سراعا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (يخرجون). Likewise (كأنهم إلى نصب) is also in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying (خاشعة): also a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (يخرجون), and likewise (ترهقهم ذلة).
